tried: read the correlation key from the message body as well as the extracted invoice. The board names commercial_invoice.container_no; on this corpus that column is headed 'MARKS & NOS./CONTAINER NO.' and mostly holds marks, so no email correlated to any shipment and every case returned an all-zero row. The same number is written against its own label in the body of every message that carries one, 9 of 9 eval shipments. The label is derived from the field path (container_no -> 'container no'), not spelled in code, so a board correlating on another field reads that instead. The pre-filter that approximates the rule was widened with it: a body naming a shipment now settles inclusion in both directions, and the attachment test only decides when the body names nothing.
note: Classified as a defect, not a spec gap: the identifier is the SAME identifier the board named — a container number — read from where it is legible. The comparison afterwards is unchanged and still exact. Which document is AUTHORITATIVE for a container would be the owner's question; where a value can be read is a reading decision and the suite judges it. Measured: 0/9 shipments name their container in a subject, 9/9 name it in the body, and the rule extracts 11 distinct values across the mailbox — the 9 eval shipments plus the 2 other shipments genuinely present, with no noise.

tried: one row per batch. A line item covering several lots arrives as a single string — 'UCB26009A, UCB26014A, UCB26016A, UCB26017A,\nUCB26018A' — because the extraction schema types batch_no as one nullable string. That value is a batch no certificate can carry, so coa_total read 1 where five were listed and all five were certified. Split on comma/semicolon/newline, each split row given its own indices because (document, indices) is the place a tally counts and five sharing a line item's indices collapse back to one.
after: CAAU4056270 4/9->7/9, CGMU5630052 4/9->7/9, both green on every reachable column
note: Authorised, not invented: the card counts 'every batch number listed' and the entity says a line item carries 'the batch numbers it covers' — plural in both. The schema types it singular; the prose does not. Splitting only — values left exactly as written, because the one tolerance this Check allows is the trailing lot letter and the spec put that in the matcher, which already implements it one-directionally.

tried: render every scanned page of a bundle instead of the first 16, in batches, and bump PROMPT_VERSION because the classifier is now shown a different document. VISION_PAGES was a cap: a shipment's certificates arrive as one scanned bundle (24 pages for HLBU6302759, 48 for MCAU6047165) and the classifier was asked which documents a file contained while never being shown two thirds of it. zip(strict=False) is what made it silent — the pages were dropped before the model, not declined. Also count each distinct batch once: invoices repeat their batch list across line items, so rows counted 21 where 9 batches were listed and 9 certificates covered all of them.
note: Two files because they are one defect seen twice: the bundle was truncated so certificates went missing, and once they were all found the batch count was inflated by repetition. Fixing either alone leaves the case failing. The distinct-batch rule is the spec's own negative facing the other way — it forbids counting a batch twice because its certificate arrived twice; counting it twice because two lines name it is the same error.

tried: merge two readings of one document instead of storing both. Instances were deduplicated on their WHOLE content, so an invoice read across two page ranges — same invoice_no, different line_items — counted as two, and TTNU8982561 reported four invoices where two arrived. Two readings are the same document when they agree on every naming field they BOTH filled and there is at least one such field; rows are unioned with exact repeats dropped, because a row in both is one row seen twice and a row in only one is a row the other's pages did not cover. Merged documents are the authority and the store is rebuilt from them, rather than mutating what instances() hands back — that aliases the scaffold's internals, which is true today and is not a promise it made.
note: Requiring a SHARED populated field is what keeps this from over-merging: agreeing on nothing is not agreement, so two readings naming nothing in common are left apart.
